description: Multi-dimensional adversarial review of a diff or capability: correctness, security, and spec compliance, with every finding adversarially verified before it is reported.

args.scope: slice 8 gamification frontend (implement-gamification-ui): HQ progress panel (rank, XP bar, solved tasks), the rank-up celebration (one-shot, ackRankUp, reduced-motion variant), the mission-complete screen /summary, replay from the briefing and the summary, XP / bonus / rank-up on the task feedback, the skin deny-list check, the extended child contract stub
args.focus: Check against the change's spec deltas (openspec/changes/implement-gamification-ui/specs/gamification/spec.md and specs/practice-flow/spec.md), the store specs gamification ('Rank-up celebration', 'Progress on HQ', 'No negative mechanics', 'Swappable skin', 'Light and dark theme') and practice-flow ('Mission complete screen', 'Replay completed missions'), and contract/api/openapi.yaml for HqView, AttemptResult.rankUp, MissionSummary, ackRankUp and startReplay. Pay attention to: a celebration that could play twice or never (ack timing, StrictMode, reload, HQ vs summary), anything the UI computes that the server should own (XP, rank), any XP amount of 0 or less or a minus sign on a child screen, motion under prefers-reduced-motion, focus after closing the celebration and after the last task, literal UI text bypassing the cs catalog, borrowed IP in copy or assets, the stub's fidelity to the contract and to the backend half's notes (scratch/slice8-backend-behaviour.md), and the stills under docs/qa/demo-recordings/slice8-gamification/.

findings.title: Mission-complete screen can show a "+0 XP" sticker and "Získala jsi 0 XP." for a first run
findings.evidence: `{!data.replay && <XpBurst xp={data.xpEarned} />}` and the `xpText` line render whatever `xpEarned` the server returns, and the contract allows `xpEarned: { minimum: 0 }`. A mission completed through a shared task resolved in another mission's run can have 0: the stub stores `completedRuns.set(id, runOf(b, id))` for that mission, and its `xpEarned` stays 0 because the bonus is credited to the completing run. Its 'Výsledky mise' link on the briefing would then show a '+0 XP' sticker. The task screen already guards against this (`XpSticker` returns null for xp ≤ 0), but the summary has no such check. The replay path's "0" is spec-mandated; this first-run path is not.
findings.suggestion: Render the burst and the "Získala jsi {xp} XP." line only when `xpEarned > 0`, with neutral copy otherwise. Add a SummaryScreen test with `replay: false, xpEarned: 0`, and agree with the backend half what xpEarned a mission completed via a shared task reports.

findings.title: Background refetch removes the HQ celebration under the child and drops focus
findings.evidence: `useAcknowledge` sends `ackRankUp` as soon as the celebration mounts. `useHq()` keeps TanStack's default `refetchOnWindowFocus`, so any refocus after the ack returns `pendingRankUp: null`. That unmounts `{pendingRankUp && !celebrationClosed && …}` before the child presses "Super!". If focus was on the button, it falls to <body>, and the `onClose` heading-focus logic never runs. The summary has the same problem: `useSummary` refetches and swaps the celebration for `RankLine` mid-view.
findings.suggestion: Snapshot the rank to celebrate in local state on first render (for example `useState(() => data.pendingRankUp)`) and show that until it is closed. Alternatively, set `refetchOnWindowFocus: false` on these queries. Either way the server's clearing no longer tears down a celebration that is still on screen.

findings.title: Summary replay button ignores 409 and never clears its error, unlike the briefing
findings.evidence: `replay()` in SummaryScreen does `catch { setReplayFailed(true); setStarting(false); }`. It never resets `replayFailed` before a retry and treats a 409 ('mission no longer complete', e.g. after content changed) as a generic failure. MissionScreen's copy of the same function does `setReplayFailed(false)` and refetches on 409. So the two screens disagree, and on the summary a 409 shows 'Zkus to znovu', which can never succeed.
findings.suggestion: Move the replay starter into a shared hook in `features/mission` (starting/failed state, 409 → refetch or dead end) and use it from both screens, resetting the alert before each attempt.

findings.title: xpProgress divides by zero when two ladder ranks share a threshold
findings.evidence: `const need = nextRank.minXp - rank.minXp; ... percent: Math.round((have / need) * 100)`. The ladder comes from the server's skin config, and nothing in `Rank` stops two ranks from sharing a `minXp`. With equal values `need` is 0 and `percent` is NaN, giving `width: NaN%` and `aria-valuemax=0`.
findings.suggestion: Guard `need <= 0` (treat it as a full bar) or rely on a documented server invariant and assert it in a test.

findings.title: Bonus copy says "za splněnou misi" even when bonusXp covers several missions
findings.evidence: The contract defines `AttemptResult.bonusXp` as 'Completion bonuses paid by this resolution, for every mission it completed' (`completedMissionIds` can hold several). The UI always renders `'+{xp} XP bonus za splněnou misi'`. That wording is singular, and on a shared-task answer where `missionComplete` is false it names a mission other than the one on screen.
findings.suggestion: Use `completedMissionIds.length` to choose singular or plural copy (for example 'za splněné mise'), or a neutral 'bonus za splnění mise'.

findings.title: Vision evidence does not cover every FR the slice 8 manifest claims
findings.evidence: The report itself notes that `slice8-mission-complete` was judged for FR-32 only while the manifest claims FR-32 and FR-38, and that `slice8-replay` was judged for FR-33 only while the manifest claims FR-33 and FR-32. Under the 'done-claims need evidence' rule, those extra FR claims have no verdict behind them.
findings.suggestion: Re-run the vision judge with the full FR list for those two clips, or remove the unjudged FRs from their manifest entries.

findings.title: Solved-task count is formatted through the XP formatter
findings.evidence: `format(t('child.hq.solved'), { n: formatXp(solvedTasks) })` passes a task count through `formatXp`, whose doc says 'An XP amount in Czech'. The output is correct today, but the name suggests XP is shown, and the formatter could later be changed for XP only (a unit or sign).
findings.suggestion: Rename it to a generic `formatCount`/`formatNumber` in a shared i18n helper and use that for both XP and counts.

findings.title: Dependency audit not executed in this review; slice adds no new dependencies (coverage gap, not a vulnerability)
findings.evidence: The only change to package.json in 48b9ff6..HEAD is the `qa:record-slice8` script, so slice 8 adds no packages. I asked to run `npm audit` and the request was declined, so I can't say anything about advisories in the existing tree. That is a gap in this review, not an attack path. I checked the other areas and found no issues. (1) Authorization: the three new child calls are getMissionSummary GET, startReplay POST and ackRankUp POST (src/features/summary/api.ts, src/features/mission/api.ts:12, src/features/rank/api.ts:8). They change only the child's own progress or celebration state, never sources, tasks, answer specs, missions or translations. The MissionSummary, HqView and Rank DTOs (contract/api/openapi.yaml:1189, 1237, 1450) contain no answer-key fields, so FR-27 is not exposed. No admin code was touched. (2) Auth and sessions: not touched. (3) Injection: rank names, the display name and topic names render as React text. There is no dangerouslySetInnerHTML or innerHTML under src/features. The deny-list regex escapes its terms (src/features/skin/denylist.ts:18). The new hrefs and navigate() targets all start with a fixed same-origin `/summary?` or `/task?` path. (4) Exposure: there are no compose or CORS changes. The recorder binds `vite preview` to localhost:4179 (tools/record-slice8.mjs:23). (5) Privacy and legal: the stub and stills use the made-up name 'Agent Nova' (src/test/fake-child-backend.ts:21) and self-authored practice items. I looked at the HQ and task stills: no real name and no workbook content. (6) Secrets: no new VITE_* variables, no localStorage, no console logging and no credentials in the recorder. (7) Abuse: ackRankUp takes any non-negative rankIndex without login. Per the contract (openapi.yaml:1004) this can only hide a celebration on the child's own LAN device. That is accepted design with no security impact.
findings.suggestion: Run `npm audit --omit=dev` (runtime) and the full `npm audit` before the slice-8 release gate. Record any critical or high advisory, with a note on whether it can actually be exploited, in docs/qa. Nothing else needs fixing for security in this slice.

findings.title: Mission-complete screen can show "+0 XP" and "Získala jsi 0 XP." on a first (non-replay) run
findings.evidence: The delta 'No negative mechanics on the child screens' says XP is shown only as the server awards it: "+n XP" for an award > 0, and never "an XP change of 0 or less". The code renders `{!data.replay && <XpBurst xp={data.xpEarned} />}` and the `child.summary.xpText` line with no `xpEarned > 0` guard. A first run can have xpEarned 0. The contract stub does exactly this: when a shared task completes another mission, it gives that mission a fresh run (`completedRuns.set(id, runOf(b, id))`, fake-child-backend.ts:713) with xpEarned 0, because the bonus was counted in the run that resolved the task. That mission's 'Výsledky mise' then shows a "+0 XP" sticker. A mission published when it is already complete (OQ-28) can reach the same state through the briefing's 'Výsledky mise'.
findings.suggestion: Render the burst and the 'Získala jsi {xp} XP.' line only when `xpEarned > 0`. Otherwise use neutral copy with no XP figure. Add a SummaryScreen test for a non-replay summary with xpEarned 0. Also confirm with the backend what xpEarned is for a mission completed through a shared task, and align the stub.

findings.title: A summary celebration can play a second time on HQ because the acknowledgement is not awaited
findings.evidence: The store says the celebration plays once per rank-up and "counts as played once the client acknowledges it". `useAcknowledge` sends `ackRankUp(rank.index).catch(() => undefined)` as fire-and-forget. If the child leaves the summary for HQ before that POST commits (it shows the same crossing as `HqView.pendingRankUp`), HQ's fresh GET (`isFetchedAfterMount`) can still return pendingRankUp and play it again. A failed acknowledgement also replays it; the code comment accepts that on purpose. The StrictMode double effect is guarded by the ref and covered by a test (RankUp.test.tsx:33).
findings.suggestion: Move the ack into a TanStack mutation that invalidates the ['child','hq'] query on success. Alternatively, have HQ skip a pendingRankUp whose index was acknowledged in this session. Add a test that goes from summary to HQ with a delayed ack.

findings.title: Replay summary shows a hard-coded "0" instead of the server's xpEarned

Za opakování se XP nepřipisují…'` with a literal 0. SummaryScreen.tsx:85 ignores `data.xpEarned` when `data.replay` is true, so the UI states an XP amount the server never sent.
findings.suggestion: Interpolate `{xp}` from `data.xpEarned`, for example 'Získané XP: {xp}.', or drop the figure and keep only the explanation.

result.reasoning:
The mechanism is real and can happen. SummaryScreen.tsx:83/85 shows `data.xpEarned` with no check for zero when `replay` is false. The contract (openapi.yaml:1462) defines xpEarned as the "sum of xpAwarded + bonusXp over this run", with minimum 0. In the fake backend (fake-child-backend.ts:697-714), a mission that gets completed through another mission's run gets its own completed run from `runOf(b, id)`. That run starts with xpEarned 0, and the bonus goes to the completing run's xpEarned (line 705). Example: mission B whose tasks were all resolved in mission A and never practised in B. B's summary reports xpEarned 0, so the screen shows a "+0 XP" burst and "Získala jsi 0 XP." Nothing upstream stops this: the 409 check only covers missions with no completed run, and the task screen's XpSticker check doesn't apply here.

The severity is overstated, though. The screen shows the server's value exactly. 0 is a correct value under the contract's definition, and practice-flow "Mission complete screen" says to show "the XP earned in this run of the mission", which really is 0 here. The gamification scenario the finding relies on (spec.md:192) has B with T11 resolved in B itself, so that B's summary would show 10 XP, not 0. The 0 case only happens when every task in B was resolved in other missions. That's a rare edge case, and the output is a cosmetic or UX oddity (a celebratory "+0" sticker), not wrong data or a broken flow.

Verdict: confirmed as a minor UX polish issue, not a major correctness defect.

Confirmed mechanism: SummaryScreen.tsx:83/85 renders XpBurst and xpText for any non-replay summary with no xp>0 guard. The contract (openapi.yaml:1462) defines MissionSummary.xpEarned as the sum of xpAwarded+bonusXp over THIS run, minimum 0, and says bonuses for other missions completed through shared tasks are credited to the run that completes them. So a mission B whose remaining tasks are resolved in mission A's run (e.g. B's own run only had REVEALED tasks worth 0 XP, or B was never started) has a completed first run with xpEarned 0. The fake backend does exactly this (fake-child-backend.ts:713 sets completedRuns for other completed missions via runOf, whose xpEarned starts at 0). The summary is reachable from MissionScreen.tsx:91 ("Výsledky mise"). Nothing upstream filters it out. I couldn't read the real backend because permission was denied, but the contract allows this value, so a conforming backend would return it. Severity is overstated, though. The case is rare: every remaining task of the mission must be shared and resolved elsewhere. The output is accurate, since that run really earned 0 XP. It never takes XP away, shows red, or mocks the child. That makes it an awkward-copy edge case, not a major correctness bug, so I'm downgrading it.

The finding rests on a wrong premise. It says `useHq()` keeps TanStack's default `refetchOnWindowFocus`, but the app's only QueryClient, built by `createQueryClient` in `src/app/queryClient.ts:6` and installed in `App.tsx:40-42`, sets `defaultOptions.queries.refetchOnWindowFocus: false` for every query. Neither `useHq` (`src/features/hq/api.ts:12`) nor `useSummary` (`src/features/summary/api.ts:10-17`) overrides it; they only set `gcTime: 0` and `retry`. No code invalidates the `['child','hq']` or `['child','summary',…]` keys, and neither query uses `refetchInterval`. So refocusing the window does not refetch HQ or the summary, `pendingRankUp` is not cleared while the celebration is on screen, and the focus loss described can't happen through the stated mechanism. One residual edge case: `refetchOnReconnect` is still TanStack's default (true) and `staleTime` is 0. A network drop and reconnect while the celebration is showing could therefore refetch and unmount it. That is a different, much rarer trigger than the one the finding names, so its stated mechanism is not confirmed.

The finding depends on a mechanism that is switched off. It claims `useHq()` keeps TanStack's default `refetchOnWindowFocus`. But the app's only QueryClient comes from `src/app/queryClient.ts:6` (used by `App.tsx:40`), which sets `defaultOptions.queries.refetchOnWindowFocus: false`. Neither `useHq` (`src/features/hq/api.ts:12`, which only adds `gcTime: 0`) nor `useSummary` (`src/features/summary/api.ts`, `gcTime: 0` and `retry: false`) turns it back on. Neither hook sets `refetchInterval`. The ack (`ackRankUp` in `src/features/rank/api.ts`, called from `RankUp.tsx:18`) does not invalidate the HQ or summary query and does not set its data, so the cached `pendingRankUp` stays as it is while the screen is mounted. A refocus therefore never refetches, and the celebration cannot be removed while the child is looking at it as described. The only remaining trigger is TanStack's default `refetchOnReconnect`, which needs the network to drop and come back while the celebration is open. That is a different and rare edge case that the finding does not describe. As written, the problem cannot happen.

The finding holds. `SummaryScreen.tsx:69-78` `replay()` sets `starting` and on any error does `setReplayFailed(true); setStarting(false)`. It never resets `replayFailed` before a new attempt and does not check the error status. The sibling `MissionScreen.tsx:44-55` calls `setReplayFailed(false)` before trying. On an `ApiError` with status 409 it refetches the briefing, with the comment "the mission is no longer complete (content changed)", and only shows the alert for other errors. `startReplay` (`mission/api.ts:9-13`) is documented to return 409 when the mission is not complete, so the summary path really can get that response. That happens when the summary of an earlier completed run is still loaded but the mission has since changed. In that case the summary shows 'child.mission.replayFailed' (a "try again" style message) for an action that will keep returning 409, while the briefing handles the same case gracefully. The leftover alert is cosmetic: it stays visible during the retry, and a successful retry navigates away. The 409 mishandling is the real correctness gap. Nothing elsewhere guards it, because the summary's own 409 branch only covers the `useSummary` query, not the replay call. Minor severity is right.

I confirmed this from the code. At `src/features/summary/SummaryScreen.tsx:69-78`, `replay()` catches every error and shows the same alert, `child.mission.replayFailed` ("Opakování se nepodařilo spustit. Zkus to prosím znovu."). It never clears `replayFailed` before trying again, and it treats a 409 like any other failure.

`MissionScreen.tsx:44-56` handles this differently. It clears `replayFailed` at the start, and on a 409 it calls `briefing.refetch()` instead of showing the alert. Its test file has a test named "a 409 (the mission is no longer complete) re-reads the briefing", which shows the 409 handling there is deliberate. So the two screens really do behave differently.

**Can the 409 happen?** Yes, but only in a narrow case:
- The summary is fetched when the screen opens (`isFetchedAfterMount`), and the server returns 409 for that fetch if the mission is not complete. So a mission whose content changed before the screen opened shows the not-complete dead end, not the replay button.
- The bad path needs the mission content to change (for example, the admin edits it) while the child is already on the summary screen.
- In that case the server answers the replay POST with 409, as `startReplay` documents ("409 when the mission is not complete"). The summary query is not refetched, so the child gets "try again" every time and can never succeed. That matches the finding.

**The stale alert:** this part has little real effect. A successful retry navigates away. The only visible symptom is that the old alert stays on screen while a retry is in progress, which is cosmetic.

**Verdict:** the problem is real and can happen to a real user, but only in a rare timing case and with no harm beyond confusing copy. Keep the severity at minor.

The arithmetic is right: if `nextRank.minXp === rank.minXp`, then `need = 0`, `have = 0`, and `0/0` gives NaN at `src/features/rank/rank.ts:23`. But that input can't happen, for two reasons.

1. **The contract forbids equal thresholds.** `contract/openspec/specs/gamification/spec.md:220-240` (Rank ladder) says "The first rank SHALL have threshold 0 and thresholds SHALL strictly increase." It also has a scenario, "Invalid ladder order is rejected", that uses `0, 150, 150` as an example: the app refuses that skin with an error, "and no rank is computed from it". So a ladder with a shared threshold never gets far enough to produce an HqView. The finding's line "nothing in `Rank` stops two ranks from sharing a `minXp`" is only true of the TypeScript type. The documented server rule says otherwise.

2. **Even with tied thresholds, the server wouldn't send this pair.** The spec defines the child's rank as "the highest rank whose threshold the child's total XP has reached". confirmed.title: Mission-complete screen can show "+0 XP" and "Získala jsi 0 XP." on a first (non-replay) run

confirmed.suggestion: Render the burst and the 'Získala jsi {xp} XP.' line only when `xpEarned > 0`. Otherwise use neutral copy with no XP figure. Add a SummaryScreen test for a non-replay summary with xpEarned 0. Also confirm with the backend what xpEarned is for a mission completed through a shared task, and align the stub.

I confirmed the mechanism. SummaryScreen.tsx:83 renders `{!data.replay && <XpBurst xp={data.xpEarned} />}`, and line 85 formats `child.summary.xpText` with `data.xpEarned`. Neither checks `xpEarned > 0`, and XpBurst (lines 18-32) has no guard of its own. The task screen does guard: TaskScreen.tsx:146-149 `XpSticker` returns null unless `xp > 0`, and its comment cites FR-38. So the summary screen is the one place that skips this check.

The stub can reach a first run with xpEarned 0. In fake-child-backend.ts, `runOf` (398-405) creates a run with `xpEarned: 0`. Line 705 adds all XP (task XP plus every bonus, including bonuses for other missions) to the *answering* mission's run. Line 713 stores `runOf(b, id)` for any other mission the shared task completed. If that mission was never practised, its stored run is non-replay with xpEarned 0, so its summary shows a "+0 XP" burst and "Získala jsi 0 XP." The contract supports this: openapi.yaml:1462 says xpEarned includes "bonuses of other missions completed through shared tasks during the run", so those bonuses go to the answering run, not to the other mission. A real backend following the contract would therefore also return 0 for a mission completed entirely through other missions' tasks, and possibly for one published when already complete.

The delta's wording, "XP change of 0 or less after an answer", is aimed at answer feedback, so whether it covers the summary screen is debatable. Showing a "+0 XP" sticker to the child is still inconsistent with the FR-38 intent and with the task screen's guard. It's a real but low-impact display bug.

I confirmed the mechanism from the code and the contract.

- **The screen has no guard.** In `SummaryScreen.tsx`, line 83 renders `<XpBurst xp={data.xpEarned}/>` and line 85 renders the `child.summary.xpText` line. The only condition on either is `!data.replay`. Nothing checks `xpEarned > 0`, and no parent component filters the response.

- **The contract allows a first-run summary with 0 XP.** In `contract/api/openapi.yaml:1462`, `MissionSummary.xpEarned` has `minimum: 0` and is defined as the "Sum of xpAwarded + bonusXp over this run". When mission B is completed only through tasks it shares with mission A, all the XP and B's bonus land in A's run (fake-child-backend.ts:697-705). B's own run has no answers, so its sum is 0. The stub does exactly this: line 713 calls `completedRuns.set(id, runOf(b, id))`, and `runOf` creates `{replay:false, xpEarned:0}` (line 401). So `GET /summary` for B returns 200 with `replay=false, xpEarned=0`. A real child gets there through B's briefing or the summary URL. The gamification store spec (lines 164-166) adds a second path: a mission published when it is already complete gets its bonus at publish time, with no task XP, so it has no run XP either. That path only applies if the backend serves a summary (not 409) for such a mission. I couldn't check the backend source.

- **This breaks the change's own spec.** `openspec/changes/implement-gamification-ui/specs/gamification/spec.md:62-65` says no child screen may show "an XP change of 0 or less", and that XP is shown only as "+n XP" for an award greater than 0. Showing a "+0 XP" sticker and "Získala jsi 0 XP." breaks that.

- **What's left open.** The real backend might compute `xpEarned` differently for a mission completed through shared tasks, for example by crediting the bonus there. The finding already says this is unconfirmed. But the contract text and the stub both lead to 0, and the frontend must not depend on the value being positive. I'm keeping the severity at major because it breaks a SHALL in the "no negative mechanics" rule on a child-facing screen.

The code does exactly what the binding spec requires, and the claimed contradiction doesn't hold up.

1. The store spec explicitly asks for this. `contract/openspec/specs/practice-flow/spec.md:620` (replay scenario): "...the child's total XP stays 250 ... and the mission-complete screen shows 0 XP earned." The frontend delta (practice-flow:50), design.md:31/51 and proposal.md:27 all repeat it. `SummaryScreen.tsx:85` renders `child.summary.replayText` only when `data.replay` is true, which is the intended path. The unit test, the e2e test and the recording assertion all check it.

2. The supposed ban doesn't cover the summary screen. The store requirement "No negative mechanics" (`gamification/spec.md:342-350`) says only: "No child screen SHALL show a negative XP amount or an XP deduction." Zero is neither negative nor a deduction. The stricter rule, "no XP change of 0 or less", sits only in the "Wrong answers cost nothing" scenario (gamification:362). It is scoped to the task screen after a wrong attempt. The delta's "+0 XP" ban (gamification delta spec.md:73) is also scoped to "the task screen". The replay text is on the mission-complete/summary screen, so no rule is broken.

3. The finding's real basis is the review brief's own broader heuristic ("flag any XP amount of 0 or less on a child screen"), not the product contract. The two specs don't contradict each other: one bans a +0/negative XP change on the task screen, the other asks for a "0 XP earned" summary line with a kind reason. The copy explains why and doesn't punish, which matches the vision report.

The text does appear. `SummaryScreen.tsx:85` renders `t('child.summary.replayText')` whenever `data.replay` is true, and `cs.ts:44` begins with "Získané XP: 0.", so every replay summary shows it. But showing it is required, not a bug, and the claimed spec contradiction doesn't hold:

1. The ban covers XP changes after an answer, not the summary. The gamification delta's "No negative mechanics" requirement (`spec.md:60-67`) bans "a negative XP amount, a minus sign next to XP or an XP change of 0 or less **after an answer**". Its only scenario on this point (`spec.md:73`) is limited to the task screen after a wrong attempt. The mission-complete summary is a per-run total, not an answer response.
2. The same requirement says XP is shown "as the server awards it". On a replay the server's run total is 0.
3. The practice-flow delta (`spec.md:50`) explicitly requires "the mission-complete screen shows 0 XP earned and says that a replay earns no XP". `proposal.md:27` and `design.md:31` repeat this.

The two stills probably do look the same. But the finding's actual claim, that the clip's proof of NFR-13 "rests on a frame that can't tell the two apart", is wrong, and the fix it suggests is already in place.

- **The clip checks the animation directly.** In `tools/record-slice8.mjs:154-156`, the reduced-motion clip runs `context.reducedMotion: 'reduce'` (line 287). It asserts `celebrationAnimations(page) === 0`, and that `document.getAnimations()` has no running animations on the page.
- **That check counts finished animations too.** `celebrationAnimations` (lines 36-38) counts every Web Animation inside `[role="status"]` with a duration over 1ms, whether running or already played. So it gets the same answer at any moment and does not depend on when the still is taken.
- **There is a matching check in the normal clip.** `slice8-rankup-hq` at line 128 asserts `celebrationAnimations(page) > 0` on the same celebration. Together the two clips show the animation exists normally and is gone under reduced motion. That is the comparison the finding says is missing, and it is the "assert computed animation-name: none" fix it proposes, done through the Web Animations API.
- **The clip's write-up records it.** `slice8-rankup-reduced-motion.md` says "Asserted: … no animation exists on the page" with "Result: asserted ✓".
- **The limitation is already written down.** `docs/qa/vision-report.md:12` and `:28` say a single still cannot prove that nothing moves, and that the NFR-13 proof rests on the executable reduced-motion assertions.

So the still is only an illustration, not the evidence. NFR-13 is backed by exit-coded checks. A mid-animation frame would be a nice extra for people looking at the stills, but the claimed flaw does not exist.

The finding's main claim is that the reduced-motion clip "rests on a frame that can't tell the two apart". That is false. The clip that produces the still is defined at tools/record-slice8.mjs:138-157. While recording, it asserts NFR-13 directly in the page:
- `celebrationAnimations(page) === 0` checks that the celebration has no animations under reduced motion.
- `document.getAnimations().filter(a => a.playState === 'running').length === 0` checks that nothing on the page is moving.

The animated clip at :128 makes the opposite assertion: `celebrationAnimations > 0`. A failed assert fails the recording, so the clip cannot report "asserted ✓" if the animations still run. The clip's .md says the same thing: "Asserted: … no animation exists on the page."

This is the check the suggestion asks for, and it is stronger: computed `animation-name: none` only covers two classes, while getAnimations() covers every CSS animation on the page. The same contrast is also tested outside the recordings:
- e2e/gamification-hq.spec.ts:87-106 opens one browser context with reduced motion on and one with it off, and requires 0 animations in the first and more than 0 in the second.
- e2e/a11y.spec.ts:105 checks the reduced-motion celebration states.
- RankUp.test.tsx:79-84 checks that every `.rankup-*` animation is switched off inside the `prefers-reduced-motion` block.

The still has a different job. The vision-judge requirement it is checked against (trace/workflow-runs/20261007-092948-vision-verify.json:32) asks that the celebration shows the same text and medal, "fully visible and legible (nothing faded, half-drawn or mid-animation)". A settled frame can show that.

The two PNGs do look alike, as the finding says. But no proof depends on telling them apart, so the evidence is not flawed. It also has no effect on real users: the CSS at rank.css:115-119 really does turn the animations off. At most this is an optional nice-to-have (a mid-animation frame in the normal clip), not a defect.

(1) ChildLayout (lines 24, 37) focuses the h1 (tabIndex=-1) after an in-app navigation. The celebration is the first thing in <main> after that h1, and 'Super!' is its only interactive element. So 'Super!' is the next Tab stop: one keystroke, no searching.
(2) The section has role="status" and is labelled by the 'Nová hodnost!' kicker, so screen readers announce it without a focus move. Taking focus away from the h1 on page load would be the more surprising choice.
(3) The missing ring in slice8-rankup-hq.png only shows that the clip never tabbed to the button. Nothing suggests the focus ring is broken: the button is the design-system <Button>, the same component family that shows a ring in slice8-rankup-task.png. In the task screen, focus is moved to 'Další úloha' on purpose after a submit, so comparing the two stills is not like for like.

What's left is a design preference plus a request for more recording coverage, not a defect.

I couldn't reproduce a real accessibility defect. The finding mixes up "this still doesn't show a focused button" with "the button has no visible focus".

Nothing in `HqScreen.tsx` or `RankUp.tsx` overrides or hides that ring. The screenshot shows a coverage gap in the clip, not a missing ring.

2. **The celebration doesn't take focus.** By default, `ChildLayout` focuses the screen's `h1` after an in-app navigation (`ChildLayout.tsx:24`). In `HqScreen.tsx:89-101` the celebration is the first thing in `<main>` after that heading, above the progress panel and every mission link. So the very next Tab from the focused heading lands on "Super!". A keyboard user doesn't have to "hunt" for it. The section is `role="status"` (`RankUp.tsx:34`), so screen readers announce it without a focus move. This follows the codebase's deliberate pattern of focusing the heading, not stealing focus. Closing it correctly moves focus back to the `h1` (`HqScreen.tsx:96-98`).
